chunks: Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir عليه السلام entered the restroom and found a morsel of bread in the filth. He took it, washed it, and handed it to a servant who was with him, saying: “Keep it with you so that I may eat it when I come out.”
Then when he came out, عليه السلام said to the servant: “Where is the morsel?” He said: “I ate it, O son of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.”
So he said: “It has not settled in the stomach of anyone except that Paradise becomes obligatory for him. Go, for you are free, for I dislike employing a man from the people of Paradise.”

key_terms.الْجَنَّةُ: Paradise, promised here as a reward
key_terms.الْقَذَرِ: filth or dirt in which the bread was found
key_terms.خُبْزٍ: bread, treated here as a divine blessing deserving respect
key_terms.لُقْمَةَ: a morsel of food, specifically a small piece meant to be eaten
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٍ: an owned servant or bondsman accompanying the Imam عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام say about a morsel of bread found in filth?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام honored a discarded morsel of bread by washing and preserving it rather than letting it remain in filth. When his servant ate it, the Imam عليه السلام declared glad tidings of Paradise for him and freed him, showing reverence for blessings and noble conduct toward servants.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.49 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) entered the restroom and found a piece of bread in the filth. He took it, washed (purified) it, and handed it to a servant who was with Him, saying: 'Keep it with you for me, to eat when I come out.'

When he emerged, he asked the servant: 'Where is the piece of bread?'
(The Servant) replied: "I have eaten it, O’ son of the Messenger of Allah (sw)."
Imam (as) said: "It has not settled in the stomach of anyone except that Paradise is obligatory for him. Go, for you are free, as I dislike to employ a man from the people of Paradise”.
